scenes.title: Invisible World
scenes.text: Your body is home to trillions of microbes, and they are so small that you carry a whole unseen universe.

scenes.title: Helpful Ones
scenes.text: Most of these microbes are harmless or even helpful, helping you digest food and train your immune system.

scenes.title: Second Brain
scenes.text: Your gut holds millions of nerves and trillions of bacteria, which is why people call it your second brain.

scenes.title: Not The Same
scenes.text: Antibiotics kill bacteria but do nothing against viruses, which is why the wrong medicine will not help a cold.

scenes.title: Simple Defense
scenes.text: Washing your hands with soap breaks apart many viruses and bacteria, one of the simplest defenses we have.

scenes.title: Body Defense
scenes.text: A fever is not the enemy. Your body raises its temperature to make it harder for germs to survive.

scenes.title: Always Changing
scenes.text: Your microbiome changes with what you eat and where you live, and scientists are still discovering what it all means.

scenes.title: Your Turn
scenes.text: You are never truly alone, even when you are by yourself. What is one habit you use to stay healthy?
